To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the deposition pattern in drying sessile drops depends on the contact line motion (pinned, sticking-and-sliding, or Marangoni-driven) and on the properties of the deposited materials.

(1) the contact line of a droplet on a substrate moves during evaporation; (2) the contact-line velocity depends on both the evaporation rate and the surface properties of the substrate and the droplet; and (3) the velocity is not a constant but depends on the contact-line radius.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the deposition patterns of drying droplets are very complex and depend on a large number of parameters, which makes it very difficult to predict the final deposition pattern.

, in the case of drying sessile droplet of a Newtonian fluid on a homogeneous surface, the final deposit pattern is determined by the balance of the following three effects: (1) the pinning or slipping of the contact line; (2) the Marangoni flow in the droplet; and (3) the evaporation rate at the droplet surface.

, while there are a number of different phenomena that contribute to the final deposition pattern in a drying sessile droplet, the most significant of these is the pinning or movement (slipping) of the contact line and the associated flow field.
